text:
Supervised context cropping has clear precedents. [DA4Rec (WWW 2024)](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.11136v1) distinguishes target-preserving perturbations, including cropping, from sliding windows that change prediction targets; direct supervised augmentation can match or outperform contrastive methods. [Pay Attention to Sequence Split (2026)](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05309) separately varies prefix/suffix/window splitting, single-/multi-target supervision, and CE/BCE losses, including GRU4Rec. Splitting offers negligible gains or can hurt under multi-target CE, supporting supervision coverage as a major confound. Neither establishes the exact stochastic-prefix-removal, matched-target control requested here. A clean ablation would compare cropped contexts against full contexts using identical target positions, negatives, target weights, loss normalization, and optimizer steps; merely masking early losses also reduces supervision.

[CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2010.14395) randomly extracts contiguous subsequences—not necessarily suffixes ending at the latest interaction—to construct paired views. Its objective combines ordinary next-item prediction with a contrastive loss aligning same-sequence views and separating other sequences. Training a GRU directly to predict the unchanged next item from a retained suffix is supervised augmentation, without that contrastive objective. Cropping alone therefore provides weak grounds for novelty; any contribution would require a distinctive mechanism or controlled evidence.

Evidence specifically demonstrating harm from suffix-cropped GRU training followed by full-history inference remains unestablished in these sources. The sequence-splitting study reports prefix splitting outperforming suffix splitting overall, but does not isolate inference-length mismatch. [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643) explicitly discusses training/evaluation mismatch for BERT4Rec’s interior-mask versus appended-mask tasks; that is related evidence, not proof for GRUs. Full-history inference after cropped training is a plausible distribution-shift hypothesis requiring validation-only comparisons of full versus matching truncated contexts, using each independently trained model separately.
